name: Toolika Rani

sections.heading: Life and writing.
paragraphs: Toolika Rani is a poet in English and Hindi, a former Indian Air Force officer and an Everest climber. Her books connect several forms of exploration: the mountaineering account “Beyond That Wall”, research on the Sherpas of Solukhumbu, and poetry collections including “A Wild Flower” and “Thus Sang the Bluebirds”. She also edited “The Mountain was Abuzz”, an international anthology devoted to the Himalaya.

Her poems here ask what it means to sustain life without possessing or exhausting it. “Water” imagines service through a river’s unceasing movement, while “The Jasmine Flowers” turns the pleasure of fragrance into a question about the violence of picking. “Sustain” answers a series of imagined losses with a determination to preserve the heart’s capacity for beauty, even when the world offers little encouragement.
